summary: Round 5, doc-only again: no production logic, no new or changed assertion predicate, and the two test-facing edits (SubscriptionEventGrantTest's class javadoc and one .as() string) are corrections in the safe direction -- the retired 'no range is expressible' claim is gone from all three sites round 4 named, and the replacement text is true against source. The javadoc's falsifiability claim holds by reading: forcing decode to return RANGE_ABSENT reds aRangeStartingAtBYTEZEROIsNotMistakenForABSENT:81-82 and aV3EventSurvivesAROUNDTrip:61 here plus the golden v3 range case, so the fields are unused-but-pinned exactly as stated. Criterion 2's third wording is a real improvement: the two-request bounded read is now admissible (it was redded last round), and the codec clause now costs something -- I verified a slice-only decodeRun cannot satisfy it, because SegmentReader.read never consults codecAndFlags and the flag only exists in the directory. ANSWER TO THE CODEC QUESTION: the fixture IS buildable today. SegmentWriter:109 writes CODEC_NONE unconditionally and has no public way to emit anything else, but GoldenSegmentV1Test:109-138 already constructs precisely this segment -- patch the directory entry at PREAMBLE+44 to a non-zero int, recompute the header CRC (SegmentReader:77-79 is the only check over it), reopen -- and asserts the patched value comes back through RunEntry.codecAndFlags(). So the criterion does not demand a fixture the tree cannot build. Two majors remain, and the first is the fourth attempt you asked for: criterion 2 still pins requests at exactly two shares, and the band between them admits the runs-per-node implementation by arithmetic, not by hypothesis. The second is that criterion 2 cannot be discharged by the row's own stated ordering.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'at one run of 1,600, at most TWO requests and strictly fewer bytes; at ADR-0042's ~400-of-1,600 node share, exactly the whole-object GET')
findings.title: The request count is pinned at K=1 and K~400 only; a header GET plus ONE RANGED GET PER RUN below the crossover satisfies all four criteria and issues ~331 requests per (node, segment)
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING IMPLEMENTATION: fetch the header range once, then one ranged GET per wanted run -- 1+K requests -- whenever K <= crossover, and the whole-object GET above it. Walk the criteria. Criterion 2, share one: K=1 gives 2 requests ('at most TWO') and ~5.2 KiB ('strictly fewer bytes'). GREEN. Criterion 2, share two: K~400 is above the crossover, so it is exactly the whole-object GET, one request, no more bytes. GREEN. Criterion 2, codec: the header fetch carries the directory, so the flag is read from what was fetched and a non-CODEC_NONE segment is refused or honoured. GREEN. Criterion 2, coordinates: every slice comes from byteStart/byteLen. GREEN. Criterion 1: the crossover is measured, recorded in ADR-0044, and the branch derives from the recorded constant; the cases at K=crossover and K=crossover+1 take opposite paths. GREEN. Criteria 3 and 4 are untouched by request counts. GREEN. Now the number, using the only price the row itself cites -- research R12 (docs/research/00-problem/02-cost-model.md:299), one GET == 19.5 KiB of cross-AZ bandwidth at $0.02/GB. An 8 MiB object is ~420 GET-equivalents of bandwidth plus 1 GET; the per-run path at K runs costs (1+K) GETs + K*5.2 KiB == 1 + 1.267K GET-equivalents. They cross at K ~= 331. So an honest implementer MEASURES and RECORDS a crossover of ~331, which is below 400 and therefore satisfies the second share, and a node holding 330 runs of one segment issues 331 requests where the whole-object path issues 1. That is 331-against-1: the same runs-per-node scaling as the 401-against-1 this clause was written to kill, differing only in that it switches off before the one share that is asserted. Nothing in the criteria reds it, and the row's own note that the count is taken at the seam does not help -- the seam faithfully reports 331. WHY THE PROSE DOES NOT COVER IT: criterion 1 phrases the measurement as 'at what node share does two-requests-and-less-bandwidth beat one-request-and-more', which PRESUPPOSES the bounded path is two requests at every K. That presupposition is never promoted into an asserted relation, and the row never says what the bounded path's request count is as a function of K -- whether the K slices are unioned into one range or issued separately is the whole question and is unstated. The fix is one clause, and it costs nothing because criterion 1 already demands the K=crossover case exist: state the relation there too -- at K = crossover, AT MOST TWO requests, the same relation as K=1 -- so the bounded path's request count is asserted to be independent of K. That also makes the recorded crossover well-posed: under a two-request union the trade is bandwidth-only, under per-run GETs it is a different measurement entirely, and today a reader cannot tell which number the row is asking for.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'counted at M5.45g's byte source ... this row must WIDEN it ... the seam is asserted to be the ONLY path from ConsumerClient to bytes') against the same row's State cell, 'todo -- no dependency'
findings.title: Criterion 2's counting assertion presupposes M5.45g's seam, which does not exist and which the row records itself as not depending on -- so on the row's own stated ordering the assertion has nothing to attach to
findings.failure_scenario: The row states twice that it has no dependency and may land first ('per-node residency is M5.45h's and this row has no dependency, so it may land first'; State cell 'todo -- no dependency'). But criterion 2 counts 'at M5.45g's byte source', says 'this row must WIDEN it', and requires that seam be 'asserted to be the ONLY path from ConsumerClient to bytes'. In the tree today there is no byte source at all: ConsumerClient.decodeInto:76-92 opens delivery.segment() -- the bytes arrive WITH the delivery -- and client/src/main/java/binjava/client/ holds only ConsumerClient, ConsumerRecord, DefaultEnvelope, Delivery and SubscriptionTransport. M5.45g, which creates the seam, is 'todo -- depends on M5.45f' and is unblocked by this very commit, so the ordering M5.66 permits is real, not theoretical. If M5.66 is taken first, its owner cannot widen a seam that is not there and cannot assert one is the only path to bytes when the only path is the delivery's own array. The discharge available to them is the one this milestone has already been burned by: stand up a local test-only fetcher, count requests against it, and record criterion 2 as met -- an assertion over a harness production does not use, which is the exact shape the row warns about elsewhere ('a unit case feeding 64 pairs to one fetcher passes while production issues ~400'). Either the State cell gains 'depends on M5.45g' (which is the honest reading of criterion 2 as written), or criterion 2 names what the count is taken at when M5.45g has not landed and how that harness is tied to the production path. As written the row asserts both and they cannot both be true.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'strictly fewer bytes than the whole-object GET')
findings.title: 'Strictly fewer bytes' is an unbounded relation: a header range plus an open-ended suffix passes while fetching half the segment for one 5.2 KiB run
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING IMPLEMENTATION: header range [0, PREAMBLE+headerLen), then the open-ended range 'bytes=byteStart-' rather than [byteStart, byteStart+byteLen). That request IS expressible -- it needs no object length, which is the reason ADR-0044:88 gives for [0, objectLen) being unnameable -- and a reader might reasonably reach for it to pick up the footer in the same call. At the asserted share, one run of 1,600, if that run is not the first the bytes fetched are strictly fewer than the whole object, so the clause passes at two requests while fetching on average half the segment: ~800x amplification where the row's stated motivation is to turn 1,600x into ~1x. Tighten the relation to the bound the design actually promises and that moves with the fixture: no more than the header range plus byteLen, plus a stated constant. 'Strictly fewer' is the same weakness class the last three drafts of this criterion were fixed for, one metric over.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'the codec read from the fetched directory and HONOURED, asserted against a segment whose directory carries a NON-CODEC_NONE flag')
findings.title: The fixture is buildable today, but 'honoured' is undefined and the only meaning the tree can host is read-and-refuse -- worth saying, or the owner reads it as requiring a codec that cannot ship in format
findings.failure_scenario: Constructibility, which was the question: YES. SegmentWriter:109 writes CODEC_NONE unconditionally and exposes no way to change it, but GoldenSegmentV1Test:109-138 builds exactly this segment today -- write a real segment, putInt a non-zero sentinel at PREAMBLE+44, recompute the header CRC (SegmentReader:77-79 is the only integrity check over the directory), reopen, and RunEntry.codecAndFlags() returns it. The helper and the precedent are both in the tree, so the criterion does not demand an unbuildable fixture and the clause IS falsifiable: a slice-only decodeRun never holds the directory, so it can neither read nor act on the flag, and any case asserting behaviour keyed to it reds. What is not decidable from the row is what 'honoured' means. Decompression cannot ship in format: no compression dependency exists in the tree, java.util.zip is banned outright by check-io-seam (scripts/io_seam_scan.py:127) and its ALLOWED carve-out (:248-251) names only CRC32, CRC32C, Adler32 and Checksum, and format is not the exempt module -- so a real codec is a new dependency or a second exemption, i.e. its own row. The only meaning M5.66's owner can discharge is 'the flag is read from the fetched directory and a non-zero codec is REFUSED by name', which is enough for the clause's purpose (it makes the directory fetch necessary) and is falsifiable against the slice-only reader. One phrase in the criterion -- 'honoured, or refused by name, and the fixture is a byte-patched directory entry, as GoldenSegmentV1Test already builds' -- keeps the next reader from costing the row a codec.
